findings.title: D6's premise is an unreachable parser state, and its prescribed fix would render a false degraded notice
findings.description: `parse_review_output` sets `fallback_used=True` in exactly two branches (src/squadron/review/parsers.py:993 and the mismatch branch), and neither can produce the state D6 describes. The mismatch branch is `verdict in (Verdict.CONCERNS, Verdict.FAIL) and not findings` — it excludes PASS by construction, so "a PASS parsed with `fallback_used=True` (verdict read, findings not)" cannot occur. The only capped run that can carry `fallback_used=True` is a *derived* PASS (verdict UNKNOWN derived from findings that did parse) — and there the findings were extracted, so D6's fix ("the `fallback_used` notice renders whenever `fallback_used` is set, after any findings") would append `_findings_not_parsed_section("A verdict of X was parsed, but no findings could be extracted…")` to an artifact whose findings parsed — a false claim of exactly the class #72/#61 removed; the same false "verdict parsed, findings did not." would print from `_display_terminal`. SC7 is consequently testable only with a hand-built fixture no production path produces. The real capped-plus-degraded interaction the design should address instead: when the cap fires on a derived verdict, D5 overwrites `verdictSource` DERIVED→IMPOSED, and since `fallback_used` is JSON-only (src/squadron/review/models.py comment on the stop-reason fields), the human-readable artifact loses every trace that the verdict was not stated by the model. Re-derive D6 (drop it, or re-scope it to the derived→imposed provenance loss) and rewrite SC7 accordingly.

findings.title: D2 does not specify the "diff key present but diff body empty" case
findings.description: When `inputs` carries a `diff` key but `_run_git_diff` returns None (its git-failure path logs a WARNING and returns None), no diff injection occurs and D2's rule — stated only for "inputs has no `diff` key" — does not say whether `diff_injection` is None (key absent; a gate reads "no diff" though one was requested) or `DiffInjection(total, 0)` per D3's worst-case logic. Thin in practice because `EmptyDiffError` guards the no-changed-files case upstream, but the tri-state is the gate contract, so the choice should be stated.

findings.title: "Two `review_client` call sites" — only one production call site exists
findings.description: Implementation Notes step 2 says "Update its two `review_client` call sites"; a grep of `src/` shows a single call site (src/squadron/review/review_client.py:154). I could not verify `test_convention_root.py`/`test_injection_decision.py` as direct `_inject_file_contents` callers (only tests/review/test_content_injection.py confirmed). Minor, but an implementer hunting a second call site wastes time — verify the count and the test-file list before task breakdown.

findings.title: The cap changes loop convergence for `until: review.pass` pipelines; the design discusses only the checkpoint path
findings.description: D4 argues via `CheckpointTrigger.ON_CONCERNS`, but a pipeline loop gated on `review.pass` whose diff stays truncated and unread will now re-review each round until `loop.max` and exit through `on_exhaust` (910's semantics) instead of silently converging — the intended fail-visible direction, and `CONCERNS` is a valid member everywhere that consumes verdicts (`_aggregate_verdicts`' rank dict, `LoopCondition.REVIEW_CONCERNS_OR_BETTER`), but the retry is futile until the config or diff changes. Recording that consequence in D4 or the risk section would complete the picture.
